newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Delifrance Asia wants bigger pie in Asia market.
newsitem.headline: Delifrance Asia wants bigger pie in Asia market.

text.p: Delifrance Asia Ltd, a French-style cafe-bakeries chain, said on Monday funds raised from its public listing will help it expand in the Asia Pacific region.

"With the funds raised from the initial public offering (IPO) and with our new shareholders, we will combine them with our expertise to accelerate our expansion," managing director Hugues Prince told reporters and analysts at a briefing.
Delifrance Asia plans to offer 45.16 million shares in its initial IPO at a price of Singapore $0.78 cents each.
Prince highlighted strategies to help the company realise its vision of "operating its business in every country in the Asia Pacific and also to secure a market leadership position."
"We want to continue to expand in the existing markets through higher penetration and to multiply our range of products and concepts to enlarge our markets," he said.
Prince said funds raised will help accelerate Delifrance geographical expansion through the setting up of more outlets in the region, and to expand its franchise and licensing programmes.
The company currently has retail outlets in Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and China and wholsale and franchising operations in Australia and the Philippines.
Tang Fook Meng, the company's regional financial controller, said over the past five years, Singapore has accounted for a major portion of group turnover.
In the fiscal year ended June 1996, Singapore accounted for over 45 percent of turnover, Tang said. He said retail sales accounted for 82 percent of turnover and wholesale 17 percent.

He said the increase in retail sales over the years is due mainly to the growth in number of outlets. Retail outlets operated by the group or under franchise and licences have increased from 39 in 1992 to 123 to date, he said.
Tang said the company's good performance is expected to continue in coming years, citing an average growth of 27.7 percent in group turnover over the past five years.
